name: SophieStam
body: My current drawing assignment involves making three versions of one character, with only the hair color changing between the finished images. The outfit is mostly blue, the background is quiet, and the final drawings will often be viewed as fairly small images. The initial set includes a dark neutral, a warm copper shade, and silver, which should give me three clearly different directions. For background vocabulary, I saved a link from my reading about a [url=https://hairstyle-guide.top]personal color test[/url] as a starting point for further reading. Those ideas may give me useful words, but a fictional drawing can deliberately exaggerate a contrast that everyday styling would soften. The issue is deciding whether the hair supports the face or distracts from it, especially when the picture is reduced in size. What sequence would you suggest for a side by side review, a value check, and a short critique from other students? A clear set of comparison questions would help my classmates explain their choices in terms of the character rather than personal taste alone.
